blocks.text: GPT Mobile Combined Mode
Design and Implementation
Reliability and performance improvements
18 October 2026   |   Design version 1.0
Prepared for Emanuel Melo and the GPT Mobile development team
Purpose and implementation decision

We will repair Combined Mode around a frozen conversation snapshot, valid provider requests, durable passage delivery, and explicit quality states. The implementation must prevent internal application messages from entering model history, preserve generated content through interruption, and make the final result clear about useful contributions and evidence verification.

The first release should address request construction and passage continuation together. Those defects determine whether selected models can answer and whether their useful content reaches the reader. Subsequent work improves repair decisions, model output handling, context size, performance visibility, and the existing Combined interface.

This specification covers the Android client, its provider adapters, Combined orchestration, persisted conversation state, and diagnostic export. It defines proposed contracts and acceptance gates for development. It does not authorize changes to user tool permissions, spending limits, or provider capacity.
Required outcomes
Every initial provider request ends in the correct role and contains the current user request once.
Every committed passage survives retry, continuation, cancellation, and application restart without silent deletion or duplication.
Useful answers, delivery completeness, request coverage, evidence verification, and attribution have separate meanings and states.
The application records where time and tokens are spent and avoids unnecessary repairs for simple exchanges.
The design uses the 18 October Combined conversation as its regression baseline and links implementation changes to repository areas and named acceptance tests. [E1]

1 Diagnostic baseline

The captured application version is 0.9.53.0, build 122. The conversation contains four user turns, twenty contributor runs, three final synthesis runs, one internal revision run, and forty two invocation records. Ten contributor runs failed. Several completed requests produced text that was unsuitable for synthesis. [E1]

Two history drafts; two unusable replies; one failure
Two history drafts; one unusable reply; two failures

blocks.text: Word counts use the exported VISIBLE_PROSE_V2 counter. Durations are approximate acceptance to stored final times, not first visible token or screen render measurements. The user supplied no explicit word limit for these turns. [E1]
Failures that determine the design

Every retained primary request includes the current pending assistant entry containing an internal notice about the merged final not being delivered. Claude rejects assistant prefill on three subsequent turns. Xiaomi returns the internal notice for both history requests. The exact provider payload is not fully captured, but the retained assembled requests and provider rejection establish the request construction defect. [E1, D1]

The Portugal continuation prompt includes an unfinished structured paragraph covering the colonial wars and the Carnation Revolution. It stops inside a JSON text string. The delivered final omits the whole section and jumps from the Estado Novo and World War II to 1986. The quality report includes INVALID_DELIVERY_RECORD. This combination strongly implicates the structured continuation path; the raw continuation response is not fully retained. [E1]

The Google Portugal invocation reports 1,966 output tokens, including 1,965 reasoning tokens, while its parent run fails for no visible answer. A completed transport request therefore cannot serve as the definition of a successful contribution. [E1]
Recorded performance and diagnostic limits

The 45.4 second greeting gap has no retained invocation or reservation explaining it. The event journal and app log snapshot are empty. Scheduling, user action, lifecycle suspension, snapshot work, and validation remain distinct hypotheses; this design does not classify the gap as a proven ANR. The manifest declares run event schema 5 while the embedded journal declares 6. [E1]

Repository reference revision da1d9dc531b17124da52309b226ec9dd419bbd8f identifies the code inspected for this design. The exported APK does not record its exact source commit. Before implementation, reconcile the listed files with the chosen development base and retain any newer compatible fixes. Future exports must include build revision and protocol versions. [R1-R8]
2 Scope and invariants

This work improves the existing Combined feature. It preserves selected profile identities, explicit user instructions, per profile tool permissions, existing conversation settings, and the meaning of any Collection and Evidence control. The implementation should reuse existing context, admission, accounting, and snapshot services rather than create a parallel execution system.

blocks.text: Boundaries

The implementation does not change the factual answers through hardcoded France or Portugal content. Those answers provide regression fixtures for generic preservation and coverage behavior. It does not silently replace selected models, enable disabled tools, make remote verification mandatory for casual chat, or promise fixed network dependent response times.

The local Assist setting remains optional. Deterministic eligibility, framing, accounting, and state validation must operate without a local model. A local or remote semantic reviewer can be used only when configured and available, and its assessment remains distinct from source verification.
3 Architecture and component ownership

Extend the existing CombinedInputSnapshot contract. At turn acceptance, persist the immutable request and selected participant identity. Seal the synthesis snapshot after selecting eligible contribution and evidence records. The coordinator owns stage transitions and the per turn completion barrier. Provider adapters own wire validation and result normalization. The delivery layer owns structured framing and durable commits. The UI renders committed state and sends explicit user actions.

blocks.text: Keep orchestration independent of whether the chat screen is composed or visible. A per turn participant set determines readiness. UI message grouping and a whole chat busy flag must not be the sole authority for starting synthesis. Cancellation and permission changes remain live controls around the frozen content snapshot.
4 Valid conversation requests
History projection

Construct initial contributor history from prior user messages and their eligible delivered assistant revisions. The current turn contains the accepted user content and attachments, with no pending assistant content. A previous Combined final should enter history once through the canonical selected revision. Individual contributor drafts remain provenance unless the user explicitly asks to inspect or compare them.

Use message origin and lifecycle metadata to identify application notices. Do not implement a global text blacklist for the internal notice string: the user may deliberately quote that string while debugging. When a previous final is partial, preserve its actual delivered content with typed delivery metadata. Do not fabricate an assistant answer for a turn that produced no usable content.

rows: Current user message last; no current assistant placeholder.
Preserve the provider specific tool call and result pairing; validate all required IDs.

Carry frozen task and relevant history plus the target revision and specific defects.
Allowed only through an explicit supported capability and dedicated caller.

blocks.text: Provider validation and admission

Add a proposed ProviderMessageValidator before RequestAdmission freezes the wire representation. Validate message roles, current user uniqueness, tool pair integrity, supported content types, and intentional prefill capability. Include validator and serializer versions in the admission receipt. A changed serialized payload requires a new receipt. [R1, R2]

For a model without prefill support, a non tool initial request ending with an assistant message fails locally with INVALID_REQUEST_ROLE before network dispatch. Treat this as a deterministic invalid request and do not retry the same bytes. The provider boundary must return a typed error with a user readable explanation and a diagnostic reason. Anthropic documents this constraint and the exact observed rejection. [D1]
Request regression cases

Exercise a new chat, an all failed previous turn, regeneration, retries after partial contributor failure, attachment input, a prior partial Combined final, a user quoting an internal notice, and process restart. Verify the final serialized messages, current user ID, and provider tail role. A unit test of only the visible prompt text is insufficient.
5 Contribution eligibility and visible output

Introduce a proposed ContributionAssessment linked to the contributor run and selected body digest. Reuse stored run and invocation identities. Persist transport outcome, normalized finish reason, visible text status, eligibility, and the exclusion reason independently. These dimensions allow the UI and synthesis planner to count useful answers without altering execution history.

blocks.text: Start with deterministic checks for typed internal output, empty visible content, provider failures, and exact prompt echo. Add a task aware relevance check only when needed to distinguish a valid short answer, requested quotation, refusal, clarification, and non answer. Any heuristic label must retain its reason and confidence; text length is not an accuracy score.

Zero eligible contributions produces a clear no usable response outcome. One eligible contribution can be delivered through Combined with accurate contributor labeling; it does not imply agreement across models. Excluded and failed profiles remain available in details. Retrying failed profiles preserves successful answers and their attempt identities.
Reasoning and response normalization

Provider normalization must collect visible text, reasoning usage, tool requests, terminal reason, and any content filtering outcome independently. A completed provider request with no visible answer remains an unsuccessful answer result. In the observed Google Portugal case, almost all reported output is reasoning; a UI rendering defect has not been demonstrated. [E1]

Use capabilities to configure reasoning and reserve visible output. If a provider does not support disabling reasoning or setting separate reasoning limits, record that fact and choose a supported recovery. Do not guess parameter names or treat hidden reasoning as displayable prose. Recovery may request a concise visible final using the same task context, with no repetition of already completed tool effects. OpenRouter exposes normalized and native finish reasons, plus distinct streaming and nonstreaming message shapes. [D2]
6 Frozen context and compact claim contracts

Extend CombinedInputSnapshot with a schema version, immutable snapshot ID, input digest, selected history revision IDs, accepted user message ID, answer contract, contribution assessments, claim references, evidence references, and protocol version. Store large bodies and provenance once, referenced by stable local IDs. A repair and its candidate answer must identify this snapshot and the revision it attempts to replace.

Later contribution or evidence changes create a successor snapshot linked to the same accepted turn; they never mutate a sealed snapshot. A repair stays bound to its original snapshot and becomes superseded if a successor replaces its selected input. Mutable delivery cursors and checkpoints belong to the delivery session keyed to that snapshot, outside the frozen content contract.

blocks.text: Context supplied to the editor

The model receives short claim and contributor IDs, the propositions, essential qualifiers, source excerpts needed for the task, and a compact relevant history. Full hashes, repeated UUIDs, ancestry arrays, and diagnostic records remain in local storage. This changes representation, not the set of eligible meanings available to the editor.
"snapshot": "S1",
"request": "history of Portugal",
"requirements": [{"id":"Q1", "kind":"chronological_overview"}],
"claims": [{"id":"K7", "text":"Example proposition",
"qualifiers":{"time":"1974"},
"contributors":["C1","C3"], "evidence":[]}]

The example is a proposed compact envelope, not a current repository API. The client resolves S1, K7, and C1 to full persisted identities. Model generated identifiers must reference the supplied inventory; unknown IDs are validation errors. Source count and inherited context are never treated as independent corroboration.
Context stability during repair

A repair receives the same relevant historical context, current request, answer contract, and eligible evidence as the original synthesis. Add the target defects and the current committed answer. Do not reconstruct context from a truncated repair prompt. Statements about earlier user requests are checked against conversation records, while external factual statements are checked against evidence.

Keep content freezing separate from permission enforcement. Recheck current permissions, spending limits, cancellation, and provider availability immediately before every dispatch. A frozen snapshot must not retain permission to execute a tool after the user disables it.
7 Resumable structured passage delivery
Protocol selection

Add a proposed PASSAGES_V3 protocol for new turns after compatibility tests pass. Preserve LEGACY_TEXT and PASSAGES_V2 readers for existing saved conversations and in progress turns. A turn keeps its selected protocol across retries and restarts. Never reinterpret a saved partial V2 record as V3.

The V3 protocol emits one complete JSON object per record. Every record type declares a sequence and stable record ID within one stream. The client supplies the target revision in the request and binds incoming records to it. The model does not choose the application revision ID or compute trusted digests.
{"type":"passage","seq":1,"id":"P0001",
"text":"A complete paragraph.",
"claims":["K1","K2"],"contributors":["C1"],"evidence":[]}
{"type":"decision","seq":2,"id":"D_K3",
"claim":"K3","disposition":"OMITTED_SCOPE",
"reason":"Outside the requested period."}
{"type":"end","seq":3,"id":"END","lastSeq":2}

Each object is transmitted as one logical record; line wrapping above is for readability. Sequence and idempotency rules apply to every record type; only passages add visible text. The end record names the preceding committed sequence in lastSeq and confirms framing completion only. The client independently assesses required scope and evidence. A model assertion cannot override sequence gaps, parser errors, or a failed request contract.
Commit and resume algorithm
Decode transport chunks into a persistent incremental record buffer. Retain partial Unicode and JSON escape state until enough bytes arrive.
Parse a complete record and validate type, expected sequence, ID, referenced claims, content length, and declared revision context.
Compute the body and record digest in the application. Persist the validated record, any associated passage, sequence, and commit event in one transaction.
Publish a committed passage to the visible answer; other records update delivery metadata. The UI never renders incomplete JSON or unvalidated fragments as accepted prose.
On interruption, persist the partial raw record separately with its expected sequence and the last committed sequence.
On continuation, regenerate the entire uncommitted record at its original sequence. Supply its partial text and claim references as recovery context, then request remaining records.
Ignore an identical replay of an already committed record. Reject a repeated ID with different content as a conflict requiring an explicit revision.
Commit completion only after the end record, sequence continuity, required scope assessment, and stage outcomes are consistent.

Use UTF8 for persisted byte digests and explicitly version the text to UTF16 offset mapping used by Android spans. Do not normalize or rewrite committed text after calculating attribution offsets. Editing a passage creates a new revision and new digests. Bound memory by spilling raw fragments to a checkpoint file when needed; preserve the fragment and report an explicit limit instead of dropping its contents.
Recovery example

In the Portugal fixture, the last valid passage concerns the Estado Novo. The next passage starts with colonial wars and the 1974 revolution but is interrupted inside its text string. The client retains the earlier passages, checkpoints this incomplete record, and requests that same record again. The regenerated section must pass the requirement and claim checks before later passages are accepted as a complete answer. [E1]

Do not use plain character overlap as the authority for passage recovery. The existing OutputLimitRecoverySession and newline decoder need a structured recovery path that preserves record identity and conflict rules. Existing plain text continuation can remain for callers that select a plain text protocol. [R3, R4]
Atomic answer repair

A repair writes to a candidate revision. Validate its framing, required topics, user constraints, attribution, and any changed evidence claims before replacing the visible revision. Commit the replacement, quality assessment, and selected revision pointer atomically. If repair is cancelled, invalid, rejected before dispatch, or incomplete, preserve the last usable visible revision with its honest partial or limited status.
8 Quality assessment and useful repairs

Replace ambiguous aggregate success with five independent quality dimensions. Completion of the provider transport is an input to delivery assessment, not the overall answer outcome. The UI may summarize the dimensions, but the stored report must retain each one and its supporting findings.

blocks.text: Required topic coverage

Build a requirement inventory from explicit user requests before synthesis. For broad requests, preserve a compact outline of the important themes or periods represented in useful contributions and identify high importance coverage candidates. A semantic planning assessment can propose this outline, but the plan must retain its source and uncertainty. Repetition by multiple models can signal a topic to consider; it does not verify the underlying claim.

A supplied, relevant section that disappears at a transport cutoff is a required delivery repair. A minor paraphrase mismatch is an attribution diagnostic. A detail outside the user scope receives an explicit omission reason. The system must distinguish these cases rather than treating all missing lexical units as equivalent.
Qualifier extraction

Classify qualifiers by grammatical role and meaning: time, amount, population, intervention route, restriction, polarity, causal strength, and evidential uncertainty. The phrase limited powers describes a restriction on authority. Limited evidence describes uncertainty. Keep those separate. Comparisons should consider the source and final clauses together, including negation and quantities. [E1]
Repair decision policy

rows: Recover the uncommitted record or repair the specific missing section.
Repair the affected structure or answer while preserving correctly covered requirements.
Correct or qualify the claim using the retained applicable evidence.
Repair metadata without requiring gratuitous prose changes.
Keep the answer and record the uncertain match in diagnostics.
Simple greeting with no factual task
Use lightweight delivery and format checks; no evidence coverage rewrite.

blocks.text: Accept a repair only when it resolves its targeted material defect and does not introduce a new required topic omission, unsupported claim, length violation, or delivery error. A metadata repair can be useful even when visible text is unchanged. Preserve accurate previously covered content and compare against the same frozen context.

Record each attempted repair, its reason, affected requirements, admission outcome, observed usage, and acceptance decision. Stop repeated identical requests when no relevant progress is made. Expose a partial outcome when a required repair cannot complete within the user limits; optional cleanup must not delay an otherwise usable greeting.
9 Evidence collection and factual verification

The existing Collection and Evidence preference, when available, controls how much source checking the workflow requests. This project preserves its stored value and meaning. It must not create a second contradictory mode or silently turn tools on. The final editor can remain a tool free pass over previously prepared material.

When checking is requested, select a configured worker whose effective permissions and live capabilities permit the required retrieval. Resolve global, profile, and conversation exclusions before dispatch. If no eligible worker exists, retain a clear evidence unavailable status and offer the relevant setting in details. A successful model response and a source count do not establish factual verification.

blocks.text: Deduplicate mirrored pages and repeated citations by canonical evidence identity when that relationship is established. Track context seen separately from proposition derived from. Blanket ancestry inherited from prior conversation should not be counted as claim specific independent evidence.

The France final contains a Tautavel age and classification inconsistent with the museum source. Use this as a fixture showing that model agreement and fluent prose cannot replace source checking. The general implementation must retrieve, compare, and cite; it must not hardcode a Tautavel correction into the editor. [E1, H1]

Use VERIFIED only for the explicitly assessed factual scope when all required checks succeed. A document with partially checked claims should show PARTIAL and identify which passages were checked. The underlying verifier can still be wrong; the label reports a completed evidence checking process and its retained support, not a guarantee of universal factual truth.
10 Adaptive output budgets and admission

The baseline uses a 2,500 token output cap for synthesis and repairs while requesting visible text plus hidden passage and decision records. The observed France and Portugal sessions reach the output limit. An output budget must account for the selected protocol and the user task, rather than assume all generated tokens become visible answer text. [E1]
Budget calculation

Estimate visible prose, structural metadata, reasoning when applicable, and continuation headroom separately. Select an allowance that fits the effective provider output capacity and remaining context, while respecting the user spending and token settings. An explicit user word limit constrains visible prose; it does not justify excluding essential metadata or increasing the answer length.

Prefer compact passage records and targeted attribution repair before increasing output allowances. A broad requested answer may require multiple permitted continuations. Continue only while required work remains, the session makes progress, and current limits allow it. A paused workflow retains the accepted partial answer and an actionable reason.

blocks.text: Typed rejection handling

Replace allowance exception handling that emits answer text followed by provider completion with a proposed RequestNotDispatched result. Include the request purpose, reason, retry disposition, relevant limit, and current usage category. Invalid roles, permission changes, capacity limits, and spending limits require different user actions. [R5]

A confirmed local rejection has zero dispatched attempts and no measured provider output. A transport failure after possible send can have unknown usage; it must not be forced to zero. Never sum parent run totals and child invocation totals as independent charges. Record the accounting source for every value used in UI totals and export.
11 Orchestration and performance
Per turn readiness

The coordinator persists the accepted participant set and each child outcome. Once required contributions and requested evidence work are terminal, it selects usable records, seals the synthesis snapshot, and starts synthesis exactly once for that snapshot. Use a durable ownership token and compare and swap transition so duplicate observer emissions or resumed workers cannot create duplicate finalization.

Distinguish intentional waiting from application overhead. A manual merge records its user action time. A paused app lifecycle, network wait, admission block, or dependency wait records a reason and start time. Once the workflow is eligible, UI grouping or rendering must not delay model dispatch without an explicit dependency.
Measurement plan

Last required contributor terminal, synthesis eligible, snapshot start and end, claim compilation start and end.

blocks.text: Use monotonic clocks for elapsed time and wall clock timestamps for cross record correlation. Separate provider first output from first visible answer because a model may first emit reasoning. Capture device, process state, protocol, snapshot size, provider route and build revision with benchmark runs.
Local work reduction

Compile a claim inventory once per sealed snapshot. Cache normalized propositions, essential qualifier extraction, requirement matching, and stable reference maps by content digest and algorithm version. For a successor snapshot, recompute only entries affected by changed contributions or evidence and reuse unchanged entries. Perform CPU intensive comparison and JSON processing off the main dispatcher.

Keep large diagnostic structures in local storage. The baseline expands about 10,986 France contributor characters into an 81,433 character synthesis envelope and 15,270 Portugal characters into a 126,197 character envelope. Compact IDs and one stored copy of provenance directly address this representation overhead. These character counts are not provider token measurements. [E1]

12 Network recovery and lifecycle states

Classify network failures by phase: DNS, connection, TLS, HTTP admission, stream transport, and response parsing. The first captured turn fails on DNS across all five contributors and records retries. It also leaves its root open despite terminal child failures. Network recovery and workflow closure must be independent, explicit operations. [E1]
Coordinated retries

Profiles sharing a connectivity failure should use one network availability decision and coordinated backoff. Preserve endpoint specific errors when only one provider is affected. Retry only the failed or unusable profiles requested by the user or permitted by current policy, while retaining successful contribution bodies and their identities.

Do not retry deterministic unsupported prefill with unchanged bytes. Do not repeat completed tool effects to recover a missing visible answer. Each retry records its failure class, parent attempt, changed request conditions, and whether a send was proven or remains uncertain.

blocks.text: An overall completed or failed root cannot contain unexplained required pending work. A resumable root may pause with blocked children and a persisted checkpoint. When all contributors fail, close that attempt with NO_USABLE_CONTRIBUTIONS or a more specific terminal outcome. A later retry creates linked new work without erasing the failed attempt.
Cancellation and restart

Cancellation stops new admissions, cancels cancellable in flight work, and preserves already committed passages. On restart, reconcile active leases and child states against persisted attempts before resuming. The cursor and passage data must be committed together so the system cannot advance past a missing paragraph after a crash.

A permission change during the turn invalidates future dispatch that depends on the revoked permission. Keep the existing committed answer and show the relevant blocked state. A provider or credential change requires new admission and may require a new semantic snapshot if the selected model or evidence scope changes.
13 User interface and interaction

Keep the ordinary Combined reading view focused on the answer. Use one compact status row within the existing response area, followed by the answer and the existing contributor navigation. Tapping the row opens details. Preserve theme colors and profile identity; color supplements a text label and never carries success or failure meaning by itself.

The copy is proposed wording for existing string resources. Offer Resume only with a valid checkpoint and a currently permitted recovery action. Blocked recovery shows the specific reason in details. Retry failed reruns eligible failed contributors while preserving successful work. A budget or permission block names the relevant setting in details.
Details view

Show each selected profile once with its useful, partial, unusable, failed, or running state. Include the exclusion reason in plain language. Separate AI contributors from retrieved evidence sources. Display delivery, request satisfaction, and evidence status without presenting one ambiguous percentage as reliability or accuracy.

Keep technical parser names, hashes, raw admission codes, token reservation structures, and the misleading 0 of 0 tool limit notice out of normal reading. They belong in debug details. A disabled tool is a capability state, not evidence that the application has exhausted completed calls.
Presentation and accessibility

Retain chronological headings and merge repeated propositions while preserving relevant unique details. Render links and citations from verified stored references. Keep the selected contributor tabs compatible with the existing bottom layout. Test compact phone widths, landscape, light and dark themes, screen reader order, and font scaling through 200 percent. Status and actions must wrap without covering the answer or composer.

Do not add new mandatory controls for protocol choice, claim IDs, token accounting, or repair loops. These are implementation decisions. Preserve the existing Collection and Evidence preference and any established per chat settings rather than adding a second settings system.
14 Diagnostics and accounting integrity

A minimum metadata journal must be available independently of full payload capture. It records lifecycle and error events needed to explain a turn while existing privacy settings continue to govern detailed content capture. Redaction must retain structural evidence such as roles, IDs, sizes, digests, outcome categories, and timing spans.

blocks.text: Export contract

Use one event schema version constant throughout the bundle manifest, conversation metadata, journal, and any nested payloads. Record an explicit journal availability reason when no events exist: disabled, not instrumented, expired by retention, or failed storage. Retained must not imply a complete event stream when the exporter has no events. [E1]

Export the captured source revision, app version, protocol version, snapshot consistency, high watermarks, gap counts, and payload capture level. Include the cause of each NOT_DISPATCHED operation and enough sanitized provider event shape to distinguish no visible output from text discarded during parsing or display.
Usage semantics

Use mutually distinguishable PROVIDER_REPORTED, ESTIMATED, RESERVED, and UNKNOWN usage categories. Preserve the provider native usage and the counting source. A reservation is a bound on allowed work, not a measurement of consumption. Missing cost data displays as unavailable or estimated with the relevant label; it must not imply free usage.

Aggregate physical attempts once. Parent run totals may summarize those attempts, but must not be added again. Record any reservation settlement and reconciliation event. A local not dispatched operation can settle at zero dispatched usage; an ambiguous network failure retains unknown usage until reliable evidence resolves it.
15 Persistence and migration

Introduce additive persistence fields and versioned readers before changing the default writer. Reuse existing Room entities and snapshot storage where they already model the needed identity. The concrete migration number must follow the repository schema at implementation time; do not reserve a guessed database version in this design.

blocks.text: Revision consistency

Use compare and swap when selecting an accepted repair: the active revision must still match the repair base revision and digest. If the user edits, regenerates, or accepts another revision first, mark the candidate superseded. Never overwrite newer user intent with a late background repair.

Transaction boundaries must keep passage text, attribution, selected revision, quality state, and continuation cursor coherent. Recovery after process death should expose either the preceding committed state or the complete new commit. It must not expose a cursor without its passage, or attribution offsets for another text revision.

Existing V2 and plain text conversations remain readable. A legacy partial stream resumes through its compatible reader or becomes a preserved partial revision with a new explicit V3 candidate. HTTP success alone is insufficient. Validate MIME type and signatures, distinguish article content from consent/login screens, detect obvious script shells, and verify required fields for structured extraction. Content length is only one signal: short legitimate pages remain valid.

Normalize scheme, hostname and default ports conservatively. Remove only reviewed tracking parameters. Preserve meaningful query values, path case and hash based application routes. A canonical URL is evidence to validate, not permission to merge different rendered documents or widen the crawl.

The queue controls permitted hosts, depth and file types. Cross-host article/PDF links may be followed only when admitted by the selected scope. DOI and paper identifiers group related resources into one study while keeping separate source URLs and document revisions.

blocks.text: Idempotency and crash recovery

Scope an idempotency key to the authenticated principal and a normalized request fingerprint. A concurrent identical start returns the same persisted job; a changed request with the same key returns IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. Enforce this with a uniqueness constraint and transaction, not an in memory map.

After a crash, reconcile expired leases and persisted network receipts before requeueing allowed reads. Never automatically restart cancelled jobs or turn an exhausted budget into a fresh allowance. A lost response may leave a network request uncertain; guarantee one committed result and one accounted receipt, not exactly one network execution.

Cancel signals browser contexts, HTTP streams and document subprocesses, then escalates after a bounded grace period. The terminal transition and result commit check the same durable generation. A completed job remains completed when a late cancel arrives. A disconnected UI can reconnect to status; automatic Combined work also requires a live, renewable parent grant and stops when that grant closes.

Combined work distinguishes coordinating tools from physical acquisition, and DeepResearchTool reserves work then checks physical request and byte receipts. Crawler must participate in the same accepted run budget. Counting one start RPC as one crawl request would undercount a multi page or browser crawl. [R13] [R14] [R15]
Budget grant and receipt protocol

The trusted app or gateway issues an immutable grant containing principal, root run, child work item, policy fingerprint, generation, request allowance, byte allowance and lease expiry. Effective limits are the minimum of the user request, parent remainder, profile policy and server capacity policy.

Persist a reservation before each outbound request and stream bytes against the remaining byte allowance. Define physicalRequests to include document reads, redirects, retries, robots files, sitemap fetches and browser subresources. Record decodedBytes separately from downloadedBytes; agree which transport level body byte counter the existing parent budget uses.

Persist monotonic cumulative receipts with unique receipt IDs and sequence numbers. The consumer applies each delta once, including after reconnects and polling replays. A coordinating wrapper is charged through its children; it must not also debit their completed work a second time.

If accounting is missing, malformed or uncertain, retain the outstanding reservation and return ACCOUNTING_UNAVAILABLE. Reconcile with the same job before retrying acquisition. Do not start an alternate engine or native fallback that could duplicate already performed work.
Browser accounting must be enforceable

Route all worker egress through one instrumented request boundary or an equivalent browser compatible accounting layer. Disable uncontrolled speculative requests, service worker bypasses and unmetered downloads. Abort a stream at the byte boundary and report partial evidence. An engine that cannot enforce a grant is not eligible for budgeted Combined acquisition; report that capability limitation during planning.

A body byte limit is an application accounting contract, not a guarantee about total network interface traffic. Track transferred body, decoded and retained bytes distinctly. Bound in flight buffers, report observed overrun or uncertainty, and never trim a receipt to make a budget appear satisfied.
Repository integration

Update the approved reader check in AndroidResearchWorkflow, the local workflow reader selection, and CombinedToolWork inspection classification together. Mark a tool coordinatesChildWork only when every acquisition is represented by child work and durable receipts. Automatic Examine inherits the accepted parent context; an explicit USER_EXAMINE action follows the app’s separate user initiated path. A model argument cannot impersonate that UI action. blocks.text: Separate acquisition from appraisal

Successful extraction creates a source available for review. It does not auto promote a source to appraised, high quality or fully read. A result may have a strong extraction signal but contain an abstract, commentary or a paywall notice. The selected review profile remains responsible for evidence assessment and the app keeps its existing provenance rules.

Do not pass every full page directly to the model. Select relevant sections from the stored revision within the accepted context budget, record which chunks were delivered, and expose continuation for additional sections. If a review depends on unavailable tables or supplementary material, preserve that limitation.
Completion and user control

Show the finished crawl and available sources before the user chooses manual Examine or archive actions, unless the accepted research plan already authorized those actions. Automatic downstream work remains under the original accepted plan and grant. Permission changes while a job is running are rechecked before new acquisition and before importing or reviewing evidence.
13 Data model and retention

Keep the durable frontier and large source artifacts on the companion server. The Android app stores connection settings, job summaries and imported evidence through its existing repositories. Crawler is an acquisition service, not a replacement for the app’s memory or Research archive.

Unique principal plus idempotency_key, linked to request fingerprint and job_id. Insertion and job creation share one transaction.
Unique job_id plus scoped URL identity; depth; priority; state; lease owner and expiry; generation. A claim requires an eligible state and valid grant.
Attempt ID; URL; engine; request IDs; stage; timestamps; error; physical request and byte counters. Receipt identity is unique and sequence increases.
Immutable document revision and content hash; artifact reference; extraction version; stable chunk offsets. Publication checks job and deletion generations.

blocks.text: Cache and content ownership

Key cached content by source identity, authenticated principal or approved public scope, credential context, render options and extraction version. Do not share private responses across profiles or callers. Record cache age and original acquisition time; cache delivery produces no new website acquisition charge, while any validation request consumes a request.

Store byte artifacts by content hash and metadata in SQLite. Bound disk use per principal and service. Retention applies independently to jobs, transient artifacts and evidence imported into the Research archive. An imported source must either have its required artifact copied into the archive or have an explicit retained reference; a routine crawl cache eviction cannot silently break a completed review.
Deletion and privacy behavior

Use deletion tombstones or generations so delayed workers and import events cannot recreate deleted content. Temporary chats use an ephemeral job and artifact retention policy rather than durable content logging. Keep diagnostics free of authorization headers, cookies, signed query strings and full private page bodies.
Resume references inherited document revisions without copying or charging them again. Its page and request limits apply to new work; report inheritedDocuments and newDocuments separately.

Use the repository’s existing theme and navigation components. Keep the primary screen in a clear single column with consistent cards, readable source previews and an obvious primary action. Progress and error states use text as well as icons or color. Long URLs wrap or ellipsize with access to the full value; no horizontal scrolling is required for normal use.

Show the requested plan and the effective plan together when policy lowers a value. Deep mode offers explicit jobs and limits rather than inheriting the quick enrichment timeout. A partial completion card names the stopping constraint and offers the relevant next action: inspect results, resume with a fresh allowance, correct scope or install an optional component.
State and permissions

Persist job IDs through rotation, process recreation and reconnects. Read permission changes before new work; disabling Crawler stops admitting new acquisition and cancels affected automatic work through its accepted parent context. Existing results remain visible according to their data permissions. Notifications reflect user meaningful job completion, not every internal worker event.
These are proposed screens and behaviors. The final implementation should reuse the repo’s actual navigation and state management conventions rather than introduce a parallel UI framework.

MarketplacePackageStore currently permits small, specifically approved assets and package types. Its 96 KiB asset and 256 KiB package limits and fixed file expectations are incompatible with shipping the crawler runtime as an ordinary mobile package. Add a reviewed companion metadata and installer route; do not simply raise those limits and download an arbitrary Python environment into the app. [R09]
Supported deployment path

The recommended first browser worker target is supported Linux, including a supported Linux distribution in WSL where appropriate. Current Playwright documentation lists Windows 11 and Windows Server 2019 or later, with WSL support; it does not establish native Windows 10 support. Validate the actual gateway and companion connection on the target server rather than promise that installing Python alone enables the browser worker. [E21]

Use a dedicated environment and data directory, configurable stdio startup or authenticated HTTP connection, and startup migrations that back up and validate the SQLite schema. Version rollback must understand the stored schema; never silently discard jobs or replay terminal work. Health reports installed, dependencies ready, service connected and a successful read probe as distinct states.

Release records include upstream notices, exact dependency locks, browser build, model manifests and optional components. Local execution avoids mandatory cloud fees; it still uses server hardware, storage and network access.
16 Errors and diagnostics

Return operation errors separately from individual source retrieval outcomes. A job may complete with useful sources and several blocked pages. Neither an empty result page nor HTTP 200 establishes successful content extraction.

Show the missing component and allowed fallback. A job can continue within policy using installed engines; record reduced capability.
Show the source access condition. Do not call it a successful article or bypass it through another engine.
Return attempt details and any partial evidence. Retry only within the shared grant and backoff policy.
Show the actual request, byte, page or deadline constraint and retained sources. Resume requires a new accepted allowance.

blocks.text: Operational visibility

Correlate app tool calls, root and child work, companion jobs, frontier items, worker attempts, document revisions and accounting receipts. Record engine versions, phase durations, cache hits, browser escalation, source outcomes, request totals and retained bytes. Redact secrets and private content from normal logs.

Provide a compact diagnostics export with configuration and error codes, explicitly selected by the user. Record service availability and engine readiness separately; a reachable MCP endpoint with a missing browser is not fully ready.
Quality signals

Track extraction coverage, relevant text retained and complete citation metadata using the evaluation corpus. Keep these measures distinct from scientific evidence appraisal. Avoid an unexplained confidence percentage; named signals such as abstract only, OCR used or missing tables are more actionable.
17 Source access and execution boundaries

Crawler accepts website content as untrusted input. The service must enforce the selected scope and work grant independently of any instructions found in a page. Retrieved text may be quoted or analyzed, but it cannot modify the job, enable tools, reveal credentials or grant itself additional access.
Navigation scope and network access

Accept supported HTTP and HTTPS URLs and validate the destination at admission, every redirect and connection. Block file and executable schemes, cloud metadata addresses, loopback and private infrastructure by default. An explicitly configured internal source allowlist may authorize intended intranet targets.

Keep crawl navigation scope separate from permitted page assets. An in scope page may require a cross origin CDN resource; allow only resources permitted by the service egress policy, with the same accounting and address checks. Follow neither arbitrary discovered hosts nor redirects into forbidden destinations.

Preserve meaningful query parameters and hash based application routes in URL identity. Strip only explicitly safe tracking parameters. A canonical link is a deduplication signal, not permission to collapse different sources or expand scope.

Use a service user agent and a shared robots policy, rate limit and Retry After handler. An access wall is a reported source outcome. Do not make CAPTCHA solving, rotating paid proxies or access bypass part of the default local plugin.
Worker and credential boundaries

Run browsers and heavy parsers in constrained processes with bounded memory, execution time and output size. Treat downloads and extracted archives as data; never execute site supplied code outside the browser sandbox or pass a URL into shell interpolation. Apply limits to decompression, PDF page counts and OCR work as well as network bytes.

Keep credential contexts separate by caller and approved source. Never inject unrelated app or model provider keys into a crawler worker. Authenticated website support is optional and explicitly configured; cookies and tokens are stored through the existing secret handling path and omitted from evidence, URLs in logs and exports.
MCP connection

For network transport, validate authentication, allowed Host and Origin values and the configured transport protection. Do not expose an unauthenticated control endpoint on a public interface. Reuse the repo’s established connection policies and cancellation boundary, with stdio as the initial service connection where practical. [R11] [E22]

The companion coordinator, Android presentation layer and Research source adapter can proceed in parallel after M0. Each uses the same checked in JSON schema and deterministic fixtures. Shared contract fixtures should cross the Python, gateway and Kotlin boundary; a Python unit test alone cannot prove that the app discovers and calls the tool correctly.
Rollout

Release an opt in companion build with explicit engine capability discovery. Existing users retain their configured tools until they enable Crawler and choose a server. Begin with public HTML and supported PDF fixtures, then broaden supported sites based on reproducible failures. Record engine versions and routing decisions in bug reports.
Definition of done

A selected online or local profile can discover Crawler, run a bounded deep job, reconnect to it, cancel or resume it, inspect verifiable sources and hand a selected revision to Examine. Physical work stays within its accepted grant, optional components fail clearly, and the app shows accurate partial completion. The acceptance matrix and performance gates below determine readiness.

21 Recovery and accounting acceptance tests

rows: A repeated key with the same normalized request returns one job. A changed request with that key fails before new work.
Lease recovery preserves one committed result and receipt. Uncertain requests remain reported; no exactly once network assumption is required.
HTTP streams, browser contexts and parser processes stop within the configured grace period. Fenced workers cannot publish content or archive events.
Resume creates one linked new job, retains parent source identities, and charges only new work. The terminal parent never reopens.
Replay across new arrivals and restart returns the same snapshot. Wrong job, scope, format or expired cursors fail explicitly.
Robots files, sitemaps, redirects, retries and browser assets all consume the shared grant. One start RPC cannot hide their work.
Chunked, compressed and unknown length bodies use measured byte counters. Boundary aborts produce partial outcomes; missing telemetry is not zero.
Receipt replay does not double debit. Missing or malformed receipts retain reservations and prevent duplicate fallback acquisition.
Automatic work stops with the accepted parent or expired grant. Explicit user Examine follows its own approved app path; model inputs cannot spoof it.
Interactive reads progress during deep crawling, background work receives its reserved share, and adapter switching cannot bypass domain backoff.
Cache eviction respects retained evidence; deletion generations prevent resurrection. Temporary jobs follow their configured ephemeral policy.
Missing browser or OCR dependencies, unsupported schema and failed migration show accurate states. Rollback preserves supported stored data.

22 Performance evaluation and release gates

No engine benchmark was run for this design. The recommendation is based on current documented capabilities and repository fit. Compare pinned builds on the intended server before claiming a speed, memory or extraction quality winner.
Evaluation corpus

Build a versioned corpus of static articles, documentation sites, JavaScript pages, short legitimate pages, tables, duplicate and tracking URLs, redirects, access walls, text PDFs and scanned PDFs. Use saved fixtures for repeatability and a small authorized live set for network realism. Include page sections and citations expected to survive extraction, with manually reviewed ground truth.

Compare retained relevant text, required sections, metadata and citations with the corpus. Report false success on access walls separately.
Record peak RSS, CPU time, browser startup, disk growth, downloaded and retained bytes, and requests per usable source.
Compare core routing with each engine forced on the same supported fixtures. Record whether escalation improves extraction enough to justify added work.
Measure crash recovery, receipt reconciliation, cancellation latency and source duplication across repeated fault injection runs.
Measure useful delivered evidence within fixed small and large context budgets. Report the tokenizer or estimate method and continuation count.

blocks.text: Proposed initial service targets

For controlled warm local fixtures, target start acknowledgement within 500 ms, status within 300 ms, and the first static source within two seconds at the evaluation concurrency. Target cancellation acknowledgement within one second and worker shutdown within ten seconds. These are engineering targets to validate and tune, not performance promises for public websites, OCR or cold browser startup.
Release gates
All AC01 through AC24 pass on the chosen supported deployment and both profile paths. Every advertised tool is callable through the real app and gateway.
The free core works without paid credentials. Dependency locks, model licences, installation, schema migration and measured capacity are recorded and reproducible.

No unaccounted acquisition, duplicate archive imports, cross principal private cache access or stale publication remains in the accepted tests. Publish effective defaults and known extraction limitations.
23 Operation schema details

The following fields define schema version 1 semantics. Check in shared JSON schemas and generated or hand verified Kotlin and Python models before implementation. Enforce numeric ranges, URL validation, output bounds and mutually exclusive start variants at the service boundary.

rows: Required url: string. Optional mode: quick or smart, default smart; query: string; format: markdown or text, default markdown; refresh: boolean, default false; maxOutputTokens: positive integer; timeoutMs: positive integer. No discovered links are scheduled.

Required seeds: nonempty string array. Optional mode: smart or deep, default deep; query; scope; sourceGoal; maxPages; maxDepth; maxPhysicalRequests; maxDownloadedBytes; deadlineMs; idempotencyKey. The client supplies a persistent key for retriable starts.

Required resumeFromJobId and a fresh idempotencyKey. Exclude seeds. Optional new limits or a narrower scope are validated under a fresh accepted grant. The caller must own the parent and have permission for retained sources.
Required jobId. Optional afterReceiptSequence supports efficient accounting reconciliation. Return cumulative totals regardless of delta optimization.
Required jobId. Optional cursor, format and maxOutputTokens. Cursor binds the job, caller scope, format, filters and snapshot. Use a fresh snapshot to observe new results.
Required jobId. Optional reason is diagnostic only and cannot change authorization. Return the durable state and latest receipt.

blocks.text: Defaults and effective plan

For the first evaluation build, propose a Deep plan of 20 desired sources, 100 admitted URLs, depth 3, 1,000 physical requests, 250 MiB of downloaded body data and a 15 minute deadline. Propose a 3,000 token result page and a 25 second fetch deadline. These defaults are visible and configurable; they are not hidden hard ceilings. An accepted parent grant can reduce them before dispatch.

Return requestedSettings and effectiveSettings with the job acknowledgement and status. Omitted settings resolve once and persist. A service policy maximum must be reported explicitly with its reason. Browser heavy sites may spend many requests on one source, so show both source and request limits.
Success and error envelopes

Return schemaVersion, operation, requestId and either data or a typed error. Individual documents carry retrievalStatus; the operation can succeed while a job outcome is partial. Output token estimation is advisory for unknown tokenizers, and an independent serialized byte limit protects the transport. A request that cannot fit even its minimal envelope fails with OUTPUT_LIMIT_TOO_SMALL.

25 Transaction and implementation notes
Admission and publication

Keep database transactions short and perform network work outside them. A frontier claim and its initial request reservation are atomic; publication verifies that the job, grant and deletion generations are still current. Browser child requests reserve through the same boundary as HTTP reads.
1. Begin a transaction, select an eligible frontier item, verify the accepted grant and scope, acquire a bounded lease, persist the attempt and initial reservation, then commit.

2. Read through the shared network boundary. Each redirect, retry or resource request obtains admission and a receipt; parsers operate on captured bytes without inventing additional physical requests.
3. Produce a candidate evidence revision and discovered links. Validate extraction coverage and destination policy before publishing or enqueueing them.
4. Begin a transaction, recheck lease ownership and generations, commit the immutable source reference, deduplicated links, event and accounting receipt, then mark the frontier item complete.
5. On timeout, crash or cancellation, reconcile the persisted attempt and measured work. Fence publication, release only proven unused reservations, and preserve uncertain work until reconciliation.

GPT Mobile Main Menu and Home Tab
Design and implementation plan
Prepared for Emanuel Melo and the GPT Mobile development team
18 October 2026
1 Purpose and delivery contract

Implement the five requested changes as one coordinated update to the main menu and Settings Home. The menu should communicate generation and unread replies through a stable icon stack, quieter profile labels, transparent folder outlines, and one shared bottom gradient. Settings Home should reuse saved OpenRouter management access, retain an event-driven wallet cache, and group selected profiles and tools inside category cards.

The implementation baseline is main at commit 9fbc60b16171fa7e7cbcae41854e8ba6f6b35d5d, reviewed on 18 October 2026. This revision contains the Settings Home work merged in PR 720. The changes below extend that implementation. Existing code observations are cited as R references; external API and platform facts are cited as E references.

Wallet means the OpenRouter account balance. A response cost is a separate value taken from its accounting receipt. Wallet active means that the Wallet category is enabled in Home configuration, including while the user is reading or generating a conversation elsewhere in the app. These definitions make the requested refresh behavior useful without requiring the Settings screen to remain open.

2 Findings in the current repository

ChatListItem currently places a 12 dp loading spinner beside a 24 dp ConversationModeSymbol. An unread subject uses Bold, without a pulse or a separate glass badge. The shared profile label helper applies 0.60 alpha in both color contrast calculation and final rendering. Those are direct local changes, but their animation and publication state must remain independent. [R1, R2]

Folder chips currently use a colored Surface fill, white text, and selected elevation. The folder entity requires one of six preset colors, and the editor defaults to the first preset. A theme-following outline cannot be expressed in the existing persistence contract. [R3, R4]

The current menu bottom fade is a scroll-dependent overlay on the chat list. It is limited to the smaller of 120 dp or 25 percent of list height. It is not a page-wide gradient. The navigation shell and Settings backdrop capture provide the appropriate integration points for a shared background. [R2, R7, R8]

The OpenRouter management credential is temporary in both provider settings and Home. connectAccountReadAccess deliberately retains no credential after its one-shot operation. Home has a separate WalletAccessDialog, and its wallet snapshot is cleared when Settings stops or is disposed. The repository already has a Keystore-backed SecretVault suitable for saving one management credential. [R9, R10, R11]

Home configuration permits profile UID entries alongside category IDs, so individual profiles use the five-item allowance. Plugins and Tools currently reports configured connection counts and a global permission flag. Actual MCP health is available from McpClientManager and persisted tool observations, but is not projected into Home. [R12, R13, R17]

The OpenRouter transport already collects generation receipts, including usage-only streaming chunks. This is the main refresh integration point. OpenRouterBatchWorker has a separate remote-response path that also needs coverage. Unread publications are a different data stream; GenerationCompletionStore.record is a compatibility no-op and must not become the wallet trigger. [R5, R14, R15, R16]

4 Profile labels and folder presentation
4 1 Profile name opacity

Change profileSubtitleColor to use one PROFILE_NAME_ALPHA value of 0.50 for both contrast evaluation and returned color. Apply that opacity once at the text layer. Do not multiply it by a second parent alpha. Route compact and expanded main-menu profile labels through the same helper, including names for Multi Chat and Combined. [R2]

Preserve the existing profile-name sanitization and theme hue treatment. Names should remain plain text without appended icons or emoji. The latest 50 percent requirement supersedes the earlier 60 percent treatment. Draft text and other supporting text keep their own typography and opacity.

Evaluate contrast against the actual local background, including the lower-screen gradient. The existing helper tries to reach a contrast ratio of 4.5 but can return its best candidate when that is impossible. A fixed alpha does not guarantee that ratio on every theme. Add a shared AppBottomGradient or equivalent theme-owned drawing primitive. Its coverage is the lower 30 percent of the root app viewport. In top-origin coordinates, darkening begins at 0.70 times the viewport height and reaches its maximum at the bottom. The 30 percent value describes height coverage, not opacity.

The intermediate values above follow a smooth interpolation between transparent and a proposed maximum scrim alpha of 0.28. Store coverage and darkness as separate tokens. val t = ((y - startY) / (viewportHeight * 0.30f)).coerceIn(0f, 1f)

Measure the shared root background before list padding and IME padding are applied. In split screen or a resized window, use that app window's viewport. Do not use LazyColumn height or full-device display metrics. The background remains anchored to the app scene while the keyboard overlays it; the chat composer and content retain their existing inset handling.

7 Saved OpenRouter management access
7 1 One credential owner

Add an OpenRouterManagementAccessRepository backed by the existing SecretVault. The provider/account settings own saving, replacing, validating, and removing management access. Home resolves that saved access through the repository and never presents a second management-key input field. [R9, R10, R11]

Use a separate managementSecretRef. Do not replace the inference credential reference used for completion requests. OpenRouter requires a management key for the credits endpoint, and management keys cannot call completion endpoints. The account wallet also differs from an inference key's spending limit. [E1, E2]

Provider settings should show whether management access is saved and offer Replace and Remove actions. On Save, perform management-role validation through the existing account client and persist the validated secret in the vault. Validation must not silently run a wallet refresh. Existing explicit provider account-read actions may update the shared cache when the user invokes them; they are not automatic Home refresh triggers.

Home shows the matching cached balance, or a concise Manage OpenRouter action if saved access is missing or invalid. Opening that action navigates to the provider configuration. Settings disposal can clear temporary form text and transient jobs, but must not delete the saved credential or successful wallet cache.

The old one-shot key cannot be recovered after it has been discarded. For an upgrade with no saved management access, provider settings may require one initial save. Once saved under the new contract, reopening or backgrounding the app must not require another entry.
7 2 Scope and credential lifecycle

Bind the management access to a stable local account connection. The credits response does not provide an account identifier in its documented response fields; the app must not infer account equivalence from a display name, model name, or key hash. Reuse an existing explicit connection association, and keep unrelated connections isolated. [E1]

Capture connection UID and account-binding revision at generation dispatch. Capture management credential revision and endpoint revision when dispatching a wallet read. A result is publishable only when those bindings still match. Never apply an old response to whichever AI profile or OpenRouter connection happens to be selected later.

Changing the management credential, account association, or endpoint invalidates incompatible wallet display immediately. Replacing an inference credential can also change its account while retaining the same connection UID. In that case, require the management-account association to be re-established unless account equivalence is independently known. Preserve the saved management secret so association repair does not require entering it again. An in-flight result from the previous scope is discarded. Removing the management credential deletes its vault record and detaches its wallet cache. Removing an inference key must not leave an orphaned reference that can be silently attached to a different account.

The existing vault encrypts records and stores them under noBackupFilesDir. Keep raw secret values out of Home preferences, UI state snapshots, event payloads, logs, and portable backup data. A restored configuration can retain display choices, but must request management access again if its protected secret is unavailable. [R11]
7 3 Wallet display contract

Continue using exact decimal parsing for total credits and total usage. Store decimal strings or a decimal type, not a floating-point amount. Compute remaining balance as total credits minus total usage, retaining negative values when returned. Round only for presentation. [R18, E1]

Show an explicit US dollar currency label, the account/connection label where needed, and the time of the last successful balance read. Hide amount affects presentation only. Use the last successful scoped cache immediately; if no cache exists, display Available after your next OpenRouter response. Do not substitute zero for missing data. [E6]

Last response cost may be shown as secondary detail from the stored receipt, including a valid zero-cost result. A missing charge remains unknown. Never subtract a receipt cost again from a freshly fetched account balance. Model catalog prices and per-key limits do not replace the account balance. [E3]

The local response cache branch must not emit a new accounting event. Any later metadata reconciliation enriches the original receipt without generating another wallet event. [R14, R15, R16]

8 2 Strict refresh policy

Read the cache when opening Home or Settings, re-entering composition, enabling Wallet, selecting a different wallet connection, foregrounding, reconnecting, or restoring the app. None of these actions automatically calls the credits endpoint.

Evaluate Wallet enablement and capture its activation revision when accepting the finalized generation event. Recheck both before dispatch. Disabling Wallet invalidates that revision, so a rapid off/on cycle cannot release old work.

For each new eligible event in a running process, allow one serialized credits request attempt when server cooldown and access rules permit. Deduplicate repeated callbacks for the same remote generation; do not collapse separate genuine responses into one request.
Do not refresh on individual tokens, tool UI updates, unread changes, or a background timer. Do not poll until a lower balance appears.
If a request fails, retain the last successful cache and its timestamp. The next qualifying response is the next automatic refresh opportunity.
Wallet failure must not delay answer visibility, fail the chat, regenerate a response, or change the provider selected for a request.

When an explicit provider settings action already fetched a matching account balance, Home can reuse that saved result. This is cache sharing, not another Home network request. Initial credential validation and ordinary navigation must not become hidden account reads.
8 3 Identity and concurrency

Assign an immutable attempt ID before each actual network generation. Include connection UID, captured account-binding revision, and the upstream generation ID when supplied. The receipt local ID should remain stable when a previously absent upstream ID becomes available. Add an alias or uniqueness rule so identity enrichment cannot create a second event.

persistOrMergeReceipt(event.identity, event.accounting)
if replayOrMetadataOnly(event) or not eligibleRemoteWork(event): return
if not walletEnabledNow(): recordSkipped(event); return
event.activationRevision = currentWalletActivationRevision()
acceptUniqueEvent(event.identity, event.capturedAccountBinding)
accountActor.enqueue(event)
accountActor.handle(event):
if not walletEnabledNow() or not scopeStillMatches(event): return
if event.activationRevision != currentWalletActivationRevision(): return
if serverCooldownActive(event.account): recordSkipped(event); return
if not atomicallyClaimDispatch(event.identity): return
result = readCreditsOnce(savedManagementAccessFor(event))
if scopeStillMatches(event): persistScopedResultOrError(result)
recordTerminalRefreshState(event.identity)

Use one application-scoped actor or mutex-controlled queue per account binding. Each accepted event also captures the Wallet activation revision; increment that revision on disable and reject mismatches before dispatch. Only one wallet request for that account is in flight. A later response remains a distinct queued event, so it cannot be lost behind an earlier fetch. Different accounts can progress independently. UI observation must not own the job lifetime.

Recheck enablement and identity before dispatch. Disabling Wallet discards pending work. A request already sent may finish and save a result for its still-valid account, but it must not re-enable the tile. Re-enabling reads cache and does not release old queued events.

Do not promise exactly-once network delivery across process death. Persist a dispatch claim before sending the request; a crash after that claim can leave an unknown result. Mark unfinished work abandoned on startup without replaying it. Preserve the previous cache and reconcile naturally after the next new qualifying response. The practical guarantee is at most one dispatch per event, with one attempt per event during normal uninterrupted operation when enabled, correctly bound, and outside a server cooldown.

The balance is an authoritative observation at its fetch time, not proof that every just-finished generation has settled. Store lastAttemptedEventSequence separately from lastSuccessfulFetchTime; avoid naming either field lastSettledGeneration. Do not claim that an unchanged returned balance means a response was free. No settlement polling is added.
8 4 Error states

Honor a server-provided Retry-After cooldown. Record events that arrive during that cooldown as skipped; do not create a timer request or replay them afterward. The first new eligible response after expiry may attempt a read. This is an explicit exception to one attempt per response during ordinary operation and keeps the user's no-polling rule intact.

Implementation plan for reliable collection analysis and final delivery
Prepared for Emanuel Melo and the GPT Mobile development team
18 October 2026
1 Decision and implementation scope

Repair Research as one durable turn that owns its accepted settings, acquisition work, source corpus, analysis, review and final delivery. The incident shows failures at several boundaries: valid Combined profile overrides are rejected by Research admission; explicit Research work is omitted from the Combined funding plan; readable evidence is not preserved in the final synthesis corpus; and a foreground service restart fails after the last contributor finishes. Fixing only search providers or raising a slider will leave the main failures in place. [E1–E5, C1–C8]

The first release should fix those boundaries, fund the required Research stages, reconcile the citation contract and keep a visible recoverable result when finalization fails. The next release should consolidate collection, improve source quality and make study cards, Examine and archive updates observable and resumable. Preserve the existing study review and archive implementation, the removal of Delegation from Combined settings, and the Evidence based to Collection and effort controls.

This plan defines repository changes and release gates. All proposed classes, new fields, targets and tests below are implementation requirements. Existing behavior is identified through the incident evidence and pinned source references.

blocks.text: 2 What the incident proves
Source acquisition and model outcomes

The app retained 44 source records representing 17 unique source IDs and URLs. Luna retained eight readable pages, including six partial reads, with 45,710 passage characters. These are source and passage counts; they do not establish 17 distinct studies or eight appraised papers. All three Research journals contain zero extracted claims and are incomplete. [E2]

All 18 Research model events were skipped with MODEL_NOT_ADMITTED, no invocation ID and zero duration: six PLAN, eight EXTRACT and four FIND_GAPS events. The source code explains why the valid Combined temperature changes trigger this rejection. The ten later OpenRouter model requests all returned HTTP 200; successful transport did not produce a valid completed Research answer. [E2, E4, C1]

Luna's writer ended at an effective 2,048 output token limit with finishReason length and zero recorded visible bytes. The export does not establish how those output tokens were used. Google and Xiaomi then failed delivery validation after repeated requests and emitted partial fallback reports. Their run status was COMPLETED while their report validation was accepted false. [E4]
The final handoff

Configuration and capture distinctions

The initial omission is proven; zero evidence in the final Luna provider request is not proven. The later Combined synthesis omission is proven by its frozen corpus. [E4, C4]

The bundle declares metadata and retained records with incomplete provider wire capture. It contains passage excerpts and body chunk references, but not those full body files or dedicated examination and archive tables. Archive failure, absent UI cards and loss of all stored full text are therefore not conclusions from this export. Initial tool catalogs are also not wire counts: the serialized initial schemas contain nine, eight and nine tools, respectively. [E1, E4]
